text.p: Shares in carmaker Renault SA were down nearly 2.5 percent in midday trading on Wednesday.
Traders offered various reasons for the drop in the share, and noted that it has become an increasingly volatile stock.
Some said it may have been hit by the disappointing results and shrinking profit margins reported on Tuesday by Fiat -- its nearest rival in Europe.

Others cited an interview on Wednesday by Industry Minister Franck Borotra in the newspaper Les Echos in which he said he hoped the French carmakers would study other options to improve productivity besides massive early retirement programmes.
"Renault is more affected because the state still has a big stake in them," a trader said. It holds 46 percent of Renault.

The French carmakers have refused to confirm newspaper reports that they are seeking government approval to cut 40,000 jobs through early retirement over several years to become more competitive but say they do want to rejuvenate their staffs. The average age of the work forces of both companies is over 40.
Renault shares were down three francs, or 2.47 percent, at 118.50 francs at 1000 GMT. PSA Peugeot Citroen shares were unchanged at 606 francs. The Paris bourse was flat.
